behavior: Device Simple mappings are compiled before global Simple in original device order. Same existing condition model and Down-bound snapshot; no additional stage.

Profile device selector normalizes missing vendor/product=0 and is_keyboard/is_pointing_device=false; ignores location/address/other type constraints as upstream factory does. Complex device_if remains explicit-field matching.
Each device batch is all-or-nothing on unsupported settings or malformed mapping; 256-device and shared 4096-mapping bounds. Windows Hook reliable-device gate unchanged.
KW-DEVICE-001 warning makes trusted fresh type-metadata dependency explicit; raw input and precise original pointer diagnostics preserved.
limitations: This is compiler/controller integration. Linux Runtime currently reports vendor/product only, not keyboard/pointing type facts; this four-field selector will not match that production context until a trusted type provider is integrated. Unknown/expired identity falls back to global Simple, never guessing false or true.
Tests inject explicit trusted ContextSnapshot data into actual engines. They do not prove native device metadata, hardware capture or output.
Device capture/ignore:true, LED, nonempty Fn and unknown hardware fields remain rejected. Only specifically recognized false no-op flags accepted.
Windows Hook cannot implement per-device input. No native Windows verification, physical input, capture or injection in this slice; previous automatic approval quota rejection remains un-retried.
